decision: Retain the qualified standalone worker and continue durable coordinator integration. Existing collectors and live execution remain unchanged.
falsifier: A surviving worker beyond tested bounds, incomplete body exposed as available, altered scope/provenance, discarded observed HTTP status, fabricated receipt time or failed reproduction reopens component qualification.
hypothesis: Independent supervisor and child deadlines plus bounded partial capture preserve public HTTP evidence without exposing incomplete bodies as responses.
limitations: Trusted local POSIX process model; no remote authentication or power-loss durability claim.
Retained decoded-byte and controlled worker lifetime bounds do not establish total-memory or hard real-time bounds.
HTTP headers are represented by observed status and timing only; raw compressed wire bytes are not retained.
Standalone invocations do not implement durable one-grant dispatch, aggregate admission, broker publication or collector continuity.
Partial HTTP 429 must be integrated with broker cooldown independently from body availability.
Physical startup delay must be included in subsequent sharing/admission replay.
